title.source: Patagonia勸少敲，1973年自己敢嗎？｜品牌故事
title.text: Patagonia's Founder Urged Fewer Pitons. Did He Dare in 1973? | Brand Story

description.source:
一個賣岩釘的人，怎麼讓攀登者相信這一錘可以少敲？從修納德親手鍛造的商品、1970年的回信與1972年型錄，走到1973年他和Bruce Carson攀登酋長岩鼻子路線的第一步。新增原始第一人稱記錄，保留楔塊移動、搭檔疑慮及後續推進的實際細節。

1974年是Carson文章刊出年，文中事件發生於1973年。1977年僅為另一採訪文章的刊出年，非已確認的到訪日。歷史畫面為匿名概念插畫，不重建真人長相、真實攀登路線或提供操作教學。

參考資料
https://publications.americanalpineclub.org/articles/12196733400/On-New-Rock-Climbing-Equipment-and-Its-Use
https://www.patagonia.com/stories/sports/climbing/a-word/story-116598.html
https://publications.americanalpineclub.org/articles/12197352200/Chouinard-Equipment
https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/1977/01/31/ascending
https://publications.americanalpineclub.org/articles/12197405800/Some-Clean-Wall-Climbs-in-Yosemite

description.text:
How does a man who sells pitons persuade climbers to use the hammer less? Follow Chouinard's hand-forged products, a 1970 reply and the 1972 catalog to the opening moves of his 1973 ascent of El Capitan's Nose with Bruce Carson. An added original first-person account preserves details of chocks moving, a partner's doubts and their subsequent progress.

Carson's article was published in 1974; the events it recounts took place in 1973. The year 1977 is only the publication year of a separate interview article, not a confirmed date for the visit. Historical scenes use anonymous conceptual illustrations; they do not reconstruct real people's appearances or actual climbing routes, or provide climbing instructions.

References

c09r5001: 一組攀岩熟手，一天能放入、取回一百枚岩釘；
下一個爬那道裂縫的人，可能就是你。
c09r5009: 這個勸告，先得穿過修納德自己賣出去的釘子。
把時間往前撥到一九五七年。
c09r5010: 他後來對記者說，那時幾乎沒人在美國做岩釘，
前輩鐵匠的貨也買不到了。
c09r5011: 早年的軟鐵釘會順著裂縫變形，
原本就不打算反覆使用；長路線得背上幾十枚。
c09r5013: 前輩做出的硬鋼釘卻能拔回來再用，
一段路爬完，器材還能跟著人繼續走。
c09r5016: 他把工具裝上車，沿加州海岸移動，
停一兩天，就生火做一批，帶到攀岩區賣。
c09r5019: 我覺得有意思的是，這麼慢做出來的東西，
還得先過買家掏錢那一關。賣多少？
c09r5020: 他說，當時歐洲岩釘約三十美分，
自己的一枚要一美元半，起初不少人嫌貴。
c09r5024: 一九六四年，第一份郵購型錄只是一張油印價目表，
還提醒五月到九月別期待迅速交貨。
c09r5027: 能買到，也開始有更多人用；但讓顧客放下它，
難處還不只是把另一件貨送進器材袋。
c09r5029: 先放釘子、接扣環和腳梯，試著承重，
再往上移動；釘子不只是在後面保護你。
c09r5030: 文章希望每枚釘子都遵循固定次序，
少拉多餘的繩索，把挪動身體的時間和力氣省下來。
c09r5031: 在這種人工攀登裡，人的重量會交給器材，
甚至連過夜的吊床，也能掛在釘子上。
c09r5033: 文章卻說，最常見的錯誤就是敲得太深；
在垂直裂縫裡，還得讓釘子抵抗轉動。
c09r5034: 它要攀登者先找合適的裂縫，
讓釘子受到自然的夾持，不是一味對著釘頭猛敲。
c09r5036: 留給稍後取釘子的人。文章提醒，
總時間要把放入和取出一起算，多補一錘可能更難回收。
c09r5039: 一九七〇年的回信被後來的採訪引出：
修納德說楔塊有用，平常卻不會拿它取代岩釘。
c09r5040: 他還嫌一位堅持用楔塊的夥伴，
放置器材花的時間，比直接敲釘子慢得多。
c09r5043: 回到開場的釘孔，型錄把原因寫得很直接：
花崗岩比合金鋼釘軟，敲拔會使薄岩片鬆落。
c09r5049: 他提出的楔塊並不是當年才出現的新發明，
英國攀岩者早就把物件卡進岩縫裡。
c09r5051: 楔塊靠形狀卡在裂縫，之後通常能取回；
少掉的，是用錘子敲入，再敲拔出來的過程。
c09r5053: 型錄請攀岩作者寫了一篇專文，
後來的採訪記下，那段使用教學有十四頁。
c09r5054: 有時，一個楔塊不夠，要兩個以上搭配；
可幾個支點，又能怎樣連成一套？
c09r5055: 採訪把這些相連的支點，比成橋樑的桁架：
幾個位置共同組合，才能把整套連接加強。
c09r5056: 原文形容，這種做法需要和岩石更親近的關係；
我覺得，讀懂眼前的裂縫才是難處。
c09r5058: 前言先說，原本已經不用岩釘的路線，
就不要再敲；其他合適路線，優先考慮可拆楔塊。
c09r5059: 真有必要用岩釘，前言提出固定留下來，
減少反覆敲拔；那後來的人怎麼知道？
c09r5062: 前言拿英國舊路線作對照：腳踩的地方早已磨亮，
沒有敲岩釘的保護裂縫，卻仍完整。
c09r5065: 一九七三年的書評，竟把七十二頁的商品型錄當書來談；
有人認為，自己的登山自由被押上了。
c09r5066: 他們說，最堅持大家換楔塊的人，
早已用岩釘爬完那些大岩壁；現在，才要求後來者改方法。
c09r5067: 這些人懷疑，那些長路線根本不可能不用岩釘完成；
如果接受這套倫理，自己就失去機會。
c09r5068: 我更想問，提出這個要求的修納德，
自己能不能帶著楔塊完成一條大岩壁路線？
c09r5070: 那位作者挖苦，付錢買型錄，
讀到的卻是買不起的器材，和自己不需要的說教。
c09r5074: 同一位書評作者也觀察到，在優勝美地，
他遇到更多堅持不帶錘子和岩釘攀登的人。
c09r5079: 他說服另一位搭檔去試，從早上攀到日落；
避開固定岩釘，卻仍用上現成螺栓。
c09r5080: 卡森在信裡說，沒了錘帶擋路，
也少了順手敲一敲、把楔塊硬塞進去的誘惑。
c09r5082: 還記得型錄裡，幾個支點組合起來的教學嗎？
這回，卡森實際用了什麼辦法？
c09r5084: 之後幾個月，他接連完成其他乾淨攀登，
累積起來，才覺得可以再試更長的路線。
c09r5086: 一九七三年八月底，卡森和修納德談起用楔塊人工攀登，
c09r5088: 開場那個器材袋，這回沒有岩釘，換成楔塊；
繩索和其他攀登裝備，仍跟著人上岩壁。
c09r5089: 過程刊在隔年的高山年刊，作者正是卡森；
兩人約定後過了兩週，修納德先往上爬。
c09r5091: 卡森寫，修納德一把重量交上去，
第一個楔塊就往下沉了約四分之一英吋，差不多六公釐。
c09r5094: 他在文章裡說，自己的心沉了下去，甚至開始盤算：
要是今天白費，明早就拿獨攀裝備出發。
c09r5095: 修納德繼續處理細裂縫，第一段也用上了幾個小型器材，
卡森跟著回收，才看出那些放置的難處。
c09r5099: 最初四段，楔塊放置費了不少功夫；
到了那處平台，日落時他們先沿繩下降。
c09r5103: 上方仍有兩段讓他們放慢腳步，
其中一處難段由修納德帶頭，另一處也得小心處理。
c09r5105: 他們比原先計畫走得快，水還很充足；
兩次過夜也都有合適岩台，能及早停下看夕陽。
c09r5106: 他們完成了這趟多日攀登。
卡森把它形容為自己最滿意的多日岩壁攀登之一。
c09r5108: 同年秋天，另一支三人隊也完成了鼻子路線的乾淨攀登，
回報沒有特別困難的楔塊放置。
c09r5109: 對卡森來說，把錘子留在家裡，
還讓熟悉大岩壁的人，重新面對攀登裡的未知。
c09r5111: 如果是你，賣家願意公開使用時的不順利，
會讓你更相信他嗎？留言告訴我。

lines.source: 一組攀岩熟手，一天能放入、取回一百枚岩釘；下一個爬那道裂縫的人，可能就是你。
lines.text: A skilled climbing team can place and retrieve a hundred pitons in a day. You might be the next person to climb that crack.

lines.source: 釘子拿走了，敲過的釘孔，卻可能留在你面前。
lines.text: The pitons are gone, but the scars from hammering may still be there in front of you.

lines.source: 把一九七二年的器材型錄攤開，旁邊放一枚鋼釘。
lines.text: Open a 1972 equipment catalog and set a steel piton beside it.

lines.source: 後來創辦Patagonia的修納德，在自家冊子裡，勸顧客克制使用器材。
lines.text: Chouinard, who would later found Patagonia, was urging customers to show restraint with equipment in his own catalog.

lines.source: 這就奇怪了：貨還要賣，原來的習慣卻得改。
lines.text: That's an odd position: he still had gear to sell, but an old habit needed to change.

lines.source: 我最想看的是，他自己站到大岩壁下，會帶什麼。
lines.text: What I most want to see is what he would pack when he stood beneath a big wall himself.

lines.source: 這回，跟著Patagonia創辦人的勸告，走到它真正承受重量的一次攀登。
lines.text: This time, we'll follow the Patagonia founder's advice to an ascent where it actually had to bear weight.

lines.source: 賣岩釘的人，做什麼才能讓你相信，這一錘可以少敲？
lines.text: What can a man who sells pitons do to convince you that you can use the hammer less?

lines.source: 這個勸告，先得穿過修納德自己賣出去的釘子。把時間往前撥到一九五七年。
lines.text: That advice first had to get past the pitons Chouinard himself had sold. Let's turn the clock back to 1957.

lines.source: 他後來對記者說，那時幾乎沒人在美國做岩釘，前輩鐵匠的貨也買不到了。
lines.text: He later told a reporter that almost nobody in America was making pitons then, and an earlier blacksmith's gear was no longer available.

lines.source: 早年的軟鐵釘會順著裂縫變形，原本就不打算反覆使用；長路線得背上幾十枚。
lines.text: Early soft-iron pitons deformed to fit cracks and weren't intended for repeated use. A long route meant carrying dozens of them.

lines.source: 前輩用過汽車前軸的鋼；這種剛硬材料，讓釘子走上了和軟鐵不同的路。
lines.text: The earlier maker had used steel from car front axles. That rigid material took pitons down a different path from soft iron.

lines.source: 前輩做出的硬鋼釘卻能拔回來再用，一段路爬完，器材還能跟著人繼續走。
lines.text: His hard-steel pitons could be pulled out and used again. After one section of a climb, the gear could keep going with you.

lines.source: 換成你，買不到合用的東西，會等別人補貨，還是自己做？
lines.text: What would you do if you couldn't buy suitable equipment: wait for someone to restock it, or make it yourself?

lines.source: 修納德買了小煤爐、鐵砧和鉗子，翻書學鍛造，開始用鉻鉬鋼做岩釘。
lines.text: Chouinard bought a small coal forge, an anvil and tongs, learned forging from books, and began making pitons from chrome-molybdenum steel.

lines.source: 他把工具裝上車，沿加州海岸移動，停一兩天，就生火做一批，帶到攀岩區賣。
lines.text: He loaded his tools into a car and traveled along the California coast. He'd stop for a day or two, fire up the forge, make a batch and sell it at climbing areas.

lines.source: 這種跟著車子走的工坊，一個鐘頭，能交出幾枚？
lines.text: How many pitons could this traveling workshop turn out in an hour?

lines.source: 照他的回憶，只有兩枚；有時他一天得守在爐前八個小時。
lines.text: By his recollection, just two. Sometimes he spent eight hours a day at the forge.

lines.source: 我覺得有意思的是，這麼慢做出來的東西，還得先過買家掏錢那一關。賣多少？
lines.text: What interests me is that something made so slowly still had to get buyers to open their wallets. What did it cost?

lines.source: 他說，當時歐洲岩釘約三十美分，自己的一枚要一美元半，起初不少人嫌貴。
lines.text: He said European pitons were about thirty cents each then, while each of his was priced at a dollar fifty. Many people initially thought that was expensive.

lines.source: 他也回憶，過了好幾年，顧客才逐漸接受，覺得這種釘子值得那個價。
lines.text: He also recalled that it took several years for customers to gradually accept that his pitons were worth the price.

lines.source: 夏天，他在攀岩區賣貨；冬天，先把下一個夏天的存貨做起來。
lines.text: In summer, he sold at climbing areas. In winter, he made stock for the following summer.

lines.source: 顧客不在眼前了，改用郵購，交貨還能跟著這個節拍走嗎？
lines.text: Once customers were ordering by mail instead of standing in front of him, could deliveries keep that same rhythm?

lines.source: 一九六四年，第一份郵購型錄只是一張油印價目表，還提醒五月到九月別期待迅速交貨。
lines.text: In 1964, the first mail-order catalog was just a mimeographed price list. It even warned against expecting prompt delivery from May through September.

lines.source: 可是訂單變多了，一枚枚靠手打，還趕得上嗎？
lines.text: But as orders grew, could he keep up by forging every piton by hand?

lines.source: 後來生產用上機器與模具，學過航空工程的夥伴，也幫忙設計製造工具。
lines.text: Production later brought in machines and dies. A partner who had studied aeronautical engineering also helped design manufacturing tools.

lines.source: 能買到，也開始有更多人用；但讓顧客放下它，難處還不只是把另一件貨送進器材袋。
lines.text: The gear became available and more people began using it. Getting customers to put it aside, though, meant more than putting a different product in their gear bags.

lines.source: 一九六七年，修納德和夥伴寫下的器材文章，已把岩釘連成一整套動作。
lines.text: By 1967, an equipment article by Chouinard and his partner had set out a whole sequence of actions around the piton.

lines.source: 先放釘子、接扣環和腳梯，試著承重，再往上移動；釘子不只是在後面保護你。
lines.text: The article described placing a piton, attaching a carabiner and aid ladder, testing it with body weight, then moving up. The piton wasn't just protection after you'd moved past it.

lines.source: 文章希望每枚釘子都遵循固定次序，少拉多餘的繩索，把挪動身體的時間和力氣省下來。
lines.text: The article called for a consistent sequence at every piton, avoiding unnecessary rope handling to save time and effort while moving the body.

lines.source: 在這種人工攀登裡，人的重量會交給器材，甚至連過夜的吊床，也能掛在釘子上。
lines.text: In this kind of aid climbing, climbers put their weight on the gear. Even an overnight hammock could hang from pitons.

lines.source: 如果你把身體交給一枚小金屬，會不會直覺以為，敲得越深越放心？
lines.text: If you entrusted your body to a small piece of metal, would you instinctively think that hammering it deeper made it safer?

lines.source: 文章卻說，最常見的錯誤就是敲得太深；在垂直裂縫裡，還得讓釘子抵抗轉動。
lines.text: Yet the article called driving pitons too deep the most common mistake. In a vertical crack, a piton also had to resist rotation.

lines.source: 它要攀登者先找合適的裂縫，讓釘子受到自然的夾持，不是一味對著釘頭猛敲。
lines.text: It asked climbers to find a suitable crack that would naturally grip the piton, rather than simply pound away at its head.

lines.source: 而且，往裡敲的那一下，還會把麻煩留給誰？
lines.text: And who else would have to deal with the consequences of that extra hammer blow?

lines.source: 留給稍後取釘子的人。文章提醒，總時間要把放入和取出一起算，多補一錘可能更難回收。
lines.text: The person removing the piton later. The article said to count both placement and removal time: one extra blow could make retrieval harder.

lines.source: 我更想知道，最熟悉這些動作的賣家自己，當時願意換嗎？
lines.text: What I want to know is whether the seller who knew those movements so well was ready to change himself.

lines.source: 一九七〇年的回信被後來的採訪引出：修納德說楔塊有用，平常卻不會拿它取代岩釘。
lines.text: A later interview quoted a reply he wrote in 1970: Chouinard said chocks were useful, but he wouldn't normally use them instead of pitons.

lines.source: 他還嫌一位堅持用楔塊的夥伴，放置器材花的時間，比直接敲釘子慢得多。
lines.text: He even complained that a partner who insisted on chocks took much longer placing gear than he would have spent hammering in pitons.

lines.source: 但他的手越來越習慣錘子，眼前的岩縫，就能一直承受下去嗎？
lines.text: But as his hands grew more accustomed to the hammer, could those cracks keep taking it forever?

lines.source: 回到開場的釘孔，型錄把原因寫得很直接：花崗岩比合金鋼釘軟，敲拔會使薄岩片鬆落。
lines.text: Back to the scars in our opening: the catalog explained the cause plainly. Granite was softer than alloy-steel pitons, and hammering them in and out loosened flakes of rock.

lines.source: 你背包裡那枚釘子還能帶回家，岩縫已經變寬，下一個人拿什麼放進去？
lines.text: You could take that piton in your pack back home, but the crack had widened. What could the next climber place there?

lines.source: 報導寫，有些原本能用小釘子的裂縫，後來得換大釘子。
lines.text: The report said some cracks that once took small pitons later needed larger ones.

lines.source: 修納德原先以為攀岩不傷害岩石，後來才承認，它可能造成很大的破壞。
lines.text: Chouinard had initially thought climbing didn't harm rock. He later acknowledged that it could do great damage.

lines.source: 他如果想讓人改掉這個動作，能只在旁邊多賣一種器材嗎？
lines.text: If he wanted people to change that action, would simply selling one more kind of gear be enough?

lines.source: 他提出的楔塊並不是當年才出現的新發明，英國攀岩者早就把物件卡進岩縫裡。
lines.text: The chocks he proposed weren't a new invention that year. British climbers had long been wedging objects into cracks.

lines.source: 從小石塊到有孔的金屬螺帽，繩子可以套住、穿過，接到攀登者這一邊。
lines.text: From small stones to metal nuts with holes, rope could go around or through them to connect them to the climber.

lines.source: 楔塊靠形狀卡在裂縫，之後通常能取回；少掉的，是用錘子敲入，再敲拔出來的過程。
lines.text: Chocks lodge in cracks because of their shape and can usually be retrieved later. What they remove is the process of hammering pitons in and hammering them out again.

lines.source: 你可能會問，知道少敲有好處，手上這件新東西，究竟怎樣才放得住？
lines.text: You might ask: knowing that less hammering is good is one thing, but how do you get this unfamiliar piece of gear to stay put?

lines.source: 型錄請攀岩作者寫了一篇專文，後來的採訪記下，那段使用教學有十四頁。
lines.text: The catalog commissioned a specialist article from a climbing writer. The later interview said those instructions ran to fourteen pages.

lines.source: 有時，一個楔塊不夠，要兩個以上搭配；可幾個支點，又能怎樣連成一套？
lines.text: Sometimes one chock wasn't enough: two or more had to work together. But how could several placements form one system?

lines.source: 採訪把這些相連的支點，比成橋樑的桁架：幾個位置共同組合，才能把整套連接加強。
lines.text: The interview compared those connected placements to a bridge truss: several positions working together to strengthen the whole connection.

lines.source: 原文形容，這種做法需要和岩石更親近的關係；我覺得，讀懂眼前的裂縫才是難處。
lines.text: The original said this approach required a closer relationship with the rock. To me, reading the crack in front of you is the difficult part.

lines.source: 可是，翻完這段，就能要求你在每一道裂縫，都做同一種選擇嗎？
lines.text: But after reading those pages, could anyone demand that you make the same choice in every crack?

lines.source: 前言先說，原本已經不用岩釘的路線，就不要再敲；其他合適路線，優先考慮可拆楔塊。
lines.text: The foreword first said not to add pitons on routes already climbed without them. On other suitable routes, removable chocks should be considered first.

lines.source: 真有必要用岩釘，前言提出固定留下來，減少反覆敲拔；那後來的人怎麼知道？
lines.text: Where pitons really were necessary, the foreword proposed leaving them fixed, reducing repeated hammering and removal. But how would later climbers know?

lines.source: 還要把位置記進當地攀登指南。
lines.text: Their locations also had to be recorded in the local climbing guide.

lines.source: 這些選擇真能讓岩壁有差別，還是只在紙上聽起來漂亮？
lines.text: Would those choices actually make a difference to the rock, or did they just sound good on paper?

lines.source: 前言拿英國舊路線作對照：腳踩的地方早已磨亮，沒有敲岩釘的保護裂縫，卻仍完整。
lines.text: The foreword pointed to old British routes: the footholds were already polished, but protection cracks that hadn't been hammered with pitons remained intact.

lines.source: 冊子把成功的尺度也改了，不只看有沒有登頂，還看人用什麼方式到達。
lines.text: The catalog also changed the measure of success: not just whether you reached the top, but how you got there.

lines.source: 但你翻到商品和價錢，會不會反問：這位賣家，憑什麼替我決定怎麼爬？
lines.text: But when you turned to the products and prices, might you ask: what gives this seller the right to tell me how to climb?

lines.source: 一九七三年的書評，竟把七十二頁的商品型錄當書來談；有人認為，自己的登山自由被押上了。
lines.text: A 1973 review treated the seventy-two-page product catalog as a book. Some people felt their freedom as climbers was at stake.

lines.source: 他們說，最堅持大家換楔塊的人，早已用岩釘爬完那些大岩壁；現在，才要求後來者改方法。
lines.text: They said the people most insistent on switching to chocks had already climbed those big walls with pitons, and were only now asking those who came after to change methods.

lines.source: 這些人懷疑，那些長路線根本不可能不用岩釘完成；如果接受這套倫理，自己就失去機會。
lines.text: Those critics doubted that the long routes could be completed without pitons. If they accepted this ethic, they would lose their chance.

lines.source: 我更想問，提出這個要求的修納德，自己能不能帶著楔塊完成一條大岩壁路線？
lines.text: My question is whether Chouinard, who was making that demand, could himself complete a big-wall route with chocks.

lines.source: 反彈也不只是年輕人。一份由年長攀岩者寫的文字，在東岸廣為流傳。
lines.text: The resistance didn't only come from younger climbers. A piece written by an older climber circulated widely on the East Coast.

lines.source: 那位作者挖苦，付錢買型錄，讀到的卻是買不起的器材，和自己不需要的說教。
lines.text: Its author mocked the idea of paying for a catalog only to read about gear he couldn't afford and receive sermons he didn't need.

lines.source: 同一位書評作者也觀察到，在優勝美地，他遇到更多堅持不帶錘子和岩釘攀登的人。
lines.text: The reviewer of the catalog also noticed that in Yosemite he was meeting more people determined to climb without hammers or pitons.

lines.source: 有人已經願意試，那位賣家會跟誰，一起走進更長的路線？
lines.text: Some were already willing to try. Who would that seller team up with to tackle a longer route?

lines.source: 後來和他搭檔的卡森，當年五月，已經在信裡寫下一次不帶錘子的嘗試。
lines.text: Carson, who would later become his partner, wrote in a May 1973 letter about an attempt without a hammer.

lines.source: 那條路線得先沿繩下降到起點；前五段爬不回來，就得過河才能離開。
lines.text: That route required rappelling down to the start. If they couldn't climb back out through the first five pitches, they'd have to cross a river to leave.

lines.source: 如果你已經到了下面，少帶一把錘子，還會只是背包裡的一點差別嗎？
lines.text: If you were already down there, would leaving out the hammer still be just a small difference in your pack?

lines.source: 他說服另一位搭檔去試，從早上攀到日落；避開固定岩釘，卻仍用上現成螺栓。
lines.text: He persuaded another partner to try. They climbed from morning until sunset, avoiding fixed pitons but still using existing bolts.

lines.source: 卡森在信裡說，沒了錘帶擋路，也少了順手敲一敲、把楔塊硬塞進去的誘惑。
lines.text: Carson wrote that without a hammer sling in the way, there was also less temptation to give a chock a quick tap and force it in.

lines.source: 第二天，另一段橫向裂縫，卻讓他遇到楔塊只能朝一個方向放的難題。
lines.text: The next day, though, a horizontal crack left him with a problem: the chocks could only be placed in one direction.

lines.source: 還記得型錄裡，幾個支點組合起來的教學嗎？這回，卡森實際用了什麼辦法？
lines.text: Remember the catalog's explanation of combining several placements? What did Carson actually do this time?

lines.source: 他先把兩件器材對向搭配，之後的支點，再一路連回最初那個位置。
lines.text: He first paired two pieces in opposing directions, then linked the later placements all the way back to that initial point.

lines.source: 之後幾個月，他接連完成其他乾淨攀登，累積起來，才覺得可以再試更長的路線。
lines.text: Over the following months, he completed more clean climbs. Only after that experience built up did he feel ready to try a longer route.

lines.source: 一九七三年八月底，卡森和修納德談起用楔塊人工攀登，約好一起去優勝美地。
lines.text: In late August 1973, Carson and Chouinard discussed aid climbing with chocks and agreed to go to Yosemite together.

lines.source: 目標是酋長岩的鼻子路線。
lines.text: Their objective was the Nose route on El Capitan.

lines.source: 開場那個器材袋，這回沒有岩釘，換成楔塊；繩索和其他攀登裝備，仍跟著人上岩壁。
lines.text: The gear bag from our opening held no pitons this time: chocks took their place. Ropes and other climbing equipment still went up the wall with them.

lines.source: 過程刊在隔年的高山年刊，作者正是卡森；兩人約定後過了兩週，修納德先往上爬。
lines.text: The account appeared in the following year's American Alpine Journal, written by Carson himself. Two weeks after making their plans, Chouinard went up first.

lines.source: 你想，他親手推薦的東西，一受重量，就會穩穩待在原地嗎？
lines.text: Would you expect the gear he'd personally recommended to stay exactly where he put it as soon as it took weight?

lines.source: 卡森寫，修納德一把重量交上去，第一個楔塊就往下沉了約四分之一英吋，差不多六公釐。
lines.text: Carson wrote that when Chouinard put his weight on the first chock, it sank about a quarter of an inch, roughly six millimeters.

lines.source: 接著，第二個楔塊一承受重量，也移動了。
lines.text: Then the second chock also moved when it took his weight.

lines.source: 兩個人以前沒一起攀登過。看見這兩步，卡森心裡怎麼想？
lines.text: The two had never climbed together before. Watching those first two moves, what went through Carson's mind?

lines.source: 他在文章裡說，自己的心沉了下去，甚至開始盤算：要是今天白費，明早就拿獨攀裝備出發。
lines.text: He wrote that his heart sank. He even began considering setting off the next morning with his solo gear if that day came to nothing.

lines.source: 修納德繼續處理細裂縫，第一段也用上了幾個小型器材，卡森跟著回收，才看出那些放置的難處。
lines.text: Chouinard continued working through thin cracks, using several small pieces on the first pitch. Following and retrieving the gear, Carson began to see the difficulty of those placements.

lines.source: 我想知道，卡森最後真的得丟下搭檔，照自己盤算的獨攀計畫走嗎？
lines.text: I want to know: did Carson really end up leaving his partner and following through on the solo plan he'd considered?

lines.source: 沒有。再過三段，他寫，兩人配合得順暢有效率，獨攀的念頭也消失了。
lines.text: No. Three pitches later, he wrote, the two were working smoothly and efficiently together, and his thoughts of soloing had disappeared.

lines.source: 最初四段，楔塊放置費了不少功夫；到了那處平台，日落時他們先沿繩下降。
lines.text: Placing chocks on the first four pitches took considerable work. At the ledge, they rappelled down at sunset.

lines.source: 更高處還等著他們。放下錘子，會不會一路都得這麼慢慢磨？
lines.text: The wall above was still waiting. Would leaving the hammer behind make the entire ascent this slow?

lines.source: 卡森記下，繼續向上時，楔塊反而更容易放，兩個人也走得更快。
lines.text: Carson recorded that as they continued upward, the chocks became easier to place, and the two climbed faster.

lines.source: 器材攀登和攀自然裂縫交錯進行；他們帶得輕，拖拉補給也沒遇到問題。
lines.text: Aid climbing alternated with climbing natural cracks. They traveled light, and hauling their supplies caused no problems.

lines.source: 上方仍有兩段讓他們放慢腳步，其中一處難段由修納德帶頭，另一處也得小心處理。
lines.text: Two sections higher up still slowed them down. Chouinard led one difficult passage, and another section also needed careful handling.

lines.source: 開頭那幾步這麼不順，最後連補給都會被拖垮嗎？
lines.text: After such an awkward start, would even their supplies become a problem by the end?

lines.source: 他們比原先計畫走得快，水還很充足；兩次過夜也都有合適岩台，能及早停下看夕陽。
lines.text: They moved faster than planned and still had plenty of water. Both overnight stops had suitable ledges, so they could stop early and watch the sunset.

lines.source: 他們完成了這趟多日攀登。卡森把它形容為自己最滿意的多日岩壁攀登之一。
lines.text: They completed the ascent over several days. Carson described it as one of his most satisfying climbs involving several days on a wall.

lines.source: 但一次搭檔順利，會不會只是剛好碰上他們兩個？
lines.text: But might one successful partnership just have been a matter of those two particular climbers?

lines.source: 同年秋天，另一支三人隊也完成了鼻子路線的乾淨攀登，回報沒有特別困難的楔塊放置。
lines.text: In autumn 1973, another team of three completed a clean ascent of the Nose, reporting no particularly difficult chock placements.

lines.source: 對卡森來說，把錘子留在家裡，還讓熟悉大岩壁的人，重新面對攀登裡的未知。
lines.text: For Carson, leaving the hammer at home brought back the unknown, even for climbers who already knew big walls well.

lines.source: 如果是你，賣家願意公開使用時的不順利，會讓你更相信他嗎？留言告訴我。
lines.text: Would you trust a seller more if they openly shared the difficulties they encountered while using the product? Let me know in the comments.

lines.source: 想看熟悉品牌的主張，怎麼經得起實際使用，歡迎訂閱這個頻道。
lines.text: Subscribe to see how familiar brands' claims stand up to actual use.
